blueprint.title: Sketch Codec Silent Corruption
blueprint.scenario: Your team ships a Go service that computes approximate quantile sketches over streaming sensor data and serialises them to a compact binary format. After a large refactor that split the original monolith into a pipeline stage library, the CI regression suite (twenty fixed inputs) still passes cleanly. But overnight the release candidate started producing wrong merge results in production: downstream dashboards show quantile estimates that drift up to 40% from the true values on high-cardinality streams. The compiled binary `/app/bin/sketchd` is the production artifact built from the refactored source tree at `/app/src/`.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
The release pipeline for `sketchd` is broken. The binary at `/app/bin/sketchd` accepts a newline-delimited stream of float64 values on stdin and, for a given sketch width, outputs a binary-encoded T-digest-style centroid list followed by a CRC32 checksum. When two sketch blobs are merged with `sketchd merge`, the merged result must satisfy these invariants on any input stream of up to 10 000 values drawn from any mixture of uniform, exponential, log-normal, or Pareto distributions:

1. The 0.5-quantile estimate of the merged sketch lies within ±2% of the true median of the combined stream.
2. The 0.05- and 0.95-quantile estimates lie within ±5% of the true 5th and 95th percentiles.
3. The CRC32 appended to every emitted blob matches the preceding bytes.
4. `sketchd merge` applied to two independently built sketches produces the same binary blob as `sketchd merge` applied in the reverse order (commutativity).

Fix the source under `/app/src/` and rebuild with `make -C /app` so the installed binary at `/app/bin/sketchd` satisfies all four invariants. Do not alter the CLI interface or the on-disk binary format.
requirements: Median estimate of merged sketch within ±2% of true median for streams up to 10 000 values
5th and 95th percentile estimates within ±5% of true values
CRC32 appended to every binary blob matches preceding content
Merge is commutative: merge(A,B) produces identical bytes to merge(B,A)
Binary at /app/bin/sketchd is rebuilt from fixed source (make -C /app succeeds)
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm installs Go 1.22 via apt, builds the project with `make -C /app` during image build, and copies the binary to /app/bin/sketchd
Source tree at /app/src/ (~1400 lines across 7 files): sketch/centroid.go, sketch/compress.go, sketch/merge.go, sketch/codec.go, pipeline/stage.go, pipeline/runner.go, cmd/main.go

sketch/merge.go contains a centroid-ordering bug introduced in the refactor: after splitting centroids from two sketches it sorts by mean but uses an unstable sort; when means are equal it breaks ties by count in descending order instead of ascending, causing the compression step to mis-cluster boundary centroids and shift tail quantiles

sketch/codec.go contains a CRC32 bug: the checksum is computed over the header bytes only (first 8 bytes) rather than the full payload, so the stored CRC passes on small sketches (where payload ≤ 8 bytes) but silently mismatches on larger ones

sketch/compress.go contains a weight-accumulation bug that only manifests when a sketch has more than 512 centroids before compression: a uint32 overflow in the running-weight field wraps around, producing a distorted compression boundary that pulls the median estimate high
The regression suite in /app/testdata/ contains 20 fixed small streams (≤200 values, all from uniform distributions) that pass all four checks even with all three bugs present
A reference Python script /app/tools/true_quantiles.py computes exact quantiles for verification
Makefile at /app builds the binary deterministically with `go build -o bin/sketchd ./cmd/`
No source for a helper binary /app/bin/streamgen that generates reproducible seeded streams is provided (it is a pre-built opaque binary used by tests at verify time to produce fresh inputs)
blueprint.internal_hint: Difficulty comes from three interacting bugs none of which is visible by inspection alone: (1) the tie-breaking sort comparator in merge.go only misbehaves when two centroids have identical means, which never happens in the 20 uniform-distribution regression streams but is common in Pareto/log-normal streams; the solver must generate high-cardinality Pareto inputs to observe it. (2) The CRC bug passes on all regression inputs because they are small enough that the payload ≤ 8 bytes; the solver must instrument the codec path or diff it against the format spec comment in codec.go which documents 'CRC32 over full frame'. (3) The uint32 overflow only triggers at >512 centroids, requiring streams of >2000 raw values; the solver has to run sketchd on a large stream and observe the median drift, then instrument compress.go. A skilled engineer (a) runs sketchd on a large Pareto stream and compares against true_quantiles.py to observe the drift, (b) bisects to the compress path by checking centroid counts before/after, (c) reads codec.go against its own inline format spec to spot the CRC scope, (d) constructs a stream with duplicate mean centroids to expose the sort tie-break. All three must be fixed for the hidden tests to pass.
blueprint.trap: A naive solver notices the CRC comment discrepancy immediately (it is the most readable clue), fixes it, rebuilds, reruns the 20 regression samples — all pass. They may also spot and fix the uint32 overflow with a large uniform stream. But the sort tie-break bug in merge.go only surfaces on Pareto/log-normal distributions where centroid means collide after the first compression pass; the hidden tests generate fresh Pareto streams at verify time and the commutativity check will fail because tie-breaking order determines which centroid absorbs mass, producing non-identical bytes and out-of-tolerance quantiles.
tests: For each of 60 verify-time streams (seeded, generated by /app/bin/streamgen with seeds 1-60, mixing uniform, exponential, log-normal and Pareto distributions, lengths 500-10000): build two non-overlapping half-streams into sketch blobs, merge them, compare 0.05/0.5/0.95 quantile estimates against true_quantiles.py output, assert all within tolerance
For each of 60 verify-time streams: compute merge(A,B) and merge(B,A) and assert the output bytes are identical
For 20 verify-time streams of length ≥3000 from Pareto(alpha=1.5) distribution: assert median estimate within ±2%
For 10 verify-time streams: assert CRC32 of the full emitted blob payload matches the stored checksum field by re-reading the binary output and recomputing the checksum independently in Python

verifier_knob.name: stream_count_and_variety
verifier_knob.effect: Reducing to 20 streams from uniform distributions only makes the task trivially passable with only the CRC fix; increasing variety and count forces all three bugs to be found

expected_failure_modes: Agent fixes only the CRC bug (most readable) and stops after regression tests pass
Agent fixes CRC and uint32 overflow but misses the sort comparator because the tie-break only triggers on non-uniform distributions not present in their self-tests
Agent rewrites merge.go entirely using a different algorithm that is correct on uniform inputs but wrong on log-normal due to a different quantile-boundary assumption
Agent changes the CLI interface or binary format while fixing the bugs, breaking the format contract checked by tests

speedrun: cat /app/src/sketch/codec.go  # spot CRC-over-header-only vs 'CRC32 over full frame' comment
cat /app/src/sketch/merge.go  # spot sort comparator with descending-count tie-break
# Edit merge.go comparator: change 'a.Count > b.Count' to 'a.Count < b.Count' for tie-break
invalid_failure_risks: streamgen is a pre-built opaque binary with no source — platform-specific failures, segfaults, or non-deterministic output would cause invalid test failures unrelated to solver correctness
Byte-exact commutativity check could fail due to non-deterministic Go runtime behavior (map iteration order, goroutine scheduling) even with a correct implementation

No on-disk binary format spec is provided to the solver; 'do not alter the binary format' invariant may be impossible to verify independently, and verifier could reject valid format-preserving changes
Go 1.22 via apt on bookworm may require internet access or specific repo pinning not described; build environment reproducibility is not guaranteed

The 20 regression samples all pass even with all three bugs, which means a solver who only runs those tests gets false confidence — but this is intended; the risk is if streamgen fails to generate the non-uniform streams needed to catch the sort bug
review.reasons: The genuine_difficulty score of 2 disqualifies this task: all three bugs are directly visible by reading the source files, and a systematic agent will find and fix all of them in ~14 commands without needing to run any non-uniform distribution tests. The 'trap' only catches agents that stop after fixing one bug and don't read the remaining files, which is not a realistic failure mode for a competent agent. Additionally, the opaque pre-built streamgen binary introduces invalid failure risk that cannot be mitigated by the solver.
fixes: Move at least one bug to a location that requires dynamic observation rather than static reading — e.g., the sort bug should be in a correct-looking comparator that only misbehaves due to a subtle numeric precision issue requiring instrumentation to detect, not a plainly wrong 'descending instead of ascending' flip

Replace the opaque pre-built streamgen binary with a Go or Python source file that is compiled/run as part of the test setup, eliminating the platform-specific binary risk and making the test environment fully reproducible from source

Add a genuine missing-implementation component (the build_component lever) that requires the solver to write new code rather than only fix existing code — e.g., the merge commutativity fix requires implementing a canonical centroid normalization step that does not exist anywhere in the current source tree

Introduce a fourth bug that requires cross-file reasoning to find — e.g., a pipeline/stage.go bug that silently truncates centroids when the pipeline buffer is exactly full, requiring the solver to trace data flow across file boundaries rather than reading each file in isolation

verdicts.reason: That task is about HMAC-SHA256 over WAL records with TCP serving and database lookups; the candidate is about fixing a T-digest sketch codec with quantile accuracy and CRC integrity.
That task involves reverse-engineering a black-box normalizer binary and fixing a SQL pipeline; the candidate is about source-level debugging of a Go sketch serialization/merge bug.
That task is black-box reverse engineering of a physics simulator in C; the candidate is white-box source repair of a Go quantile sketch library.

Both tasks involve finding a silent numerical correctness regression introduced by a refactor that the existing CI suite misses, and fixing the implementation to meet a stated accuracy threshold — the domain (spectral entropy vs. T-digest sketches) differs but the core problem structure is essentially the same.

Both tasks involve a refactored library that passes regression tests but silently produces wrong results on out-of-corpus inputs, requiring source-level debugging and a rebuild — the domain (AES-CTR encryption vs. quantile sketches) differs but the underlying challenge is identical.
